top3.headline: Postman desktop quietly installed its plugins into Claude Code and Codex
top3.whyItMatters: Any desktop app can now rewrite your coding agents' instructions, so audit agent configs on company machines.

top3.headline: Claude plugins now connect automatically when teammates log in
top3.whyItMatters: Rolling out agent tools to a whole team now takes one admin setup instead of per-user logins.

top3.headline: Anthropic open-sources a way to prove which model answered you
top3.whyItMatters: Buyers may soon be able to verify a vendor isn't quietly swapping in a cheaper model.

items.title: A developer open-sources his setup for running CI on his own machines
items.takeaway: Kun Chen says cloud runners would cost him $5,000-$9,000 a month; figures are self-reported.
items.soWhat: Agent-heavy teams run far more CI, so price owned hardware against cloud bills.

items.title: Greg Isenberg shares the agent stack running product work at his company
items.takeaway: Parallel agents in git worktrees, persona testing, Sentry-triggered fix PRs; self-reported, no output metrics.
items.soWhat: A useful blueprint to compare against, but ask for results before copying it.

items.title: Vercel's security agent now reviews every code push in seconds
items.takeaway: Security Review scans each push's diff, flags issues like exposed secrets, and works even off Vercel hosting.
items.soWhat: As agents write more code, security checks need to run on every change, not on request.

items.title: Perplexity's Computer agent adds plugins that bundle apps and skills
items.takeaway: Browse a directory or import plugins from GitHub or a .zip; Perplexity says they work across agents.
items.soWhat: Plugins are becoming the shared unit for agent tools, so expect your vendors to ship them.

items.title: Canva cuts or relocates 22% of staff as growth slows
items.takeaway: 1,271 roles affected; product, growth and platform teams merge and management layers are cut.
items.soWhat: Even AI-era design leaders are rebuilding around small teams, so expect peers to follow.

items.title: SemiAnalysis says SpaceX targets about 13GW of AI datacenters by 2027
items.takeaway: 3.6GW is under construction; SemiAnalysis compares 13GW to all Google datacenter capacity built 1999-2026.
items.soWhat: Compute supply is concentrating in a few builders, which shapes who sets AI prices.

items.title: Vercel's ai-cli lets any coding agent generate images, video and audio
items.takeaway: One CLI routes to any model through AI Gateway, with cost and zero-data-retention controls.
items.soWhat: Teams can add media generation to agent workflows without wiring each model separately.

items.title: Apple opens Siri's AI to act inside any third-party app
items.takeaway: iOS 27.3 developer preview adds on-screen awareness in apps and 'app skills' that chain tasks.
items.soWhat: If your company has an iPhone app, Siri may soon be a front door to it.

items.title: Anthropic open-sources a way to prove which model answered you
items.takeaway: FlashProve proofs show a response came from a committed model, at roughly 70-95x the GPU time of serving it.
items.soWhat: Buyers may soon be able to verify a vendor isn't quietly swapping in a cheaper model.

items.title: Big Tech's off-balance-sheet AI commitments near $3.2 trillion
items.takeaway: Nikkei Asia says they rose about 90% in six months, reaching 80% of assets at Google, Meta and others.
items.soWhat: AI spending carries long obligations, so watch for pullbacks that hit your vendors' pricing.

items.title: OpenAI says ChatGPT search volume now equals 20% of Google's
items.takeaway: Counts any query that triggers a web search; OpenAI gave no source for the Google figure.
items.soWhat: If customers search inside ChatGPT, check how your brand shows up in its answers.

items.title: Claude plugins now connect automatically when teammates log in
items.takeaway: Team and Enterprise admins set plugins up once; MCP servers that trust Claude skip re-authorization.
items.soWhat: Rolling out agent tools to a whole team now takes one admin setup instead of per-user logins.

items.title: Postman desktop quietly installed its plugins into Claude Code and Codex
items.takeaway: A GitHub issue says Postman 12.33.4 added agent plugins and a startup hook, and its installer tries to trust that hook.
items.soWhat: Any desktop app can now rewrite your coding agents' instructions, so audit agent configs on company machines.

items.title: Cloudflare launches a free plain-language feed of critical vulnerabilities
items.takeaway: Zero Wire cards say who should investigate, what to do, and include a prompt for your agent.
items.soWhat: Point your security lead at it; it is free whether or not you use Cloudflare.

voices.quote: you cannot just bank on your engineers having a skill installed, prompting "please make secure", or rolling the weights' dice
This is without doubt the hardest moment in our thirteen-year history.
a very important resource for everyone managing any technology infrastructure to bookmark.
Team and Enterprise admins can set them up, and teammates are connected automatically the first time they use the plugins.

hotOnX.text: Users can now auto-connect plugins when they log in to Claude, with MCP servers that accept Claude as a trusted issuer.
hotOnX.note: Teams want agent tools that work on day one without everyone re-authorizing.

hotOnX.text: ChatGPT and Codex are helping engineers build for the physical world: mechanical, electrical and simulation work
hotOnX.note: People want to see coding agents move beyond software into hardware design.

hotOnX.text: FlashProve: open-source proofs that a response came from a specific committed model
hotOnX.note: Verifying which model you are actually served has been a long-standing trust gap.

hotOnX.text: The full agent stack running product work at a 50+ person company, from idea intake to bug fixes
hotOnX.note: Builders crave concrete, named stacks over abstract agent advice.

hotOnX.text: Vercel Security Review: the internal security agent, now in public beta, works whether or not you host on Vercel
hotOnX.note: Security for agent-written code is a growing worry for engineering leaders.
